paragraphs: Children in care in Cheshire West and Chester are looked after by the council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council recruits through Foster4, a shared fostering service it runs with Halton and Warrington councils, so enquiries about fostering with the council locally go through Foster4.

The council has said for several years that the number of children coming into its care is growing. When it launched its Home Based Heroes campaign in November 2021 it named the groups it most needed homes for: teenagers, brothers and sisters who need to stay together, children with additional needs, and unaccompanied asylum-seeking young people, along with babies and toddlers or young parents with their newborns for carers who are at home full time.

In May 2022 Foster4 introduced support packages for council foster carers, including 24-hour local out-of-hours support, help with equipment, swimming passes and the use of a seven-seater pool car. In May 2023 the council appealed for specialist carers to give a long-term family home to children who have lived through adverse childhood experiences and might otherwise live in a children's home, with a professional fee it described at the time as £52,000 a year plus allowances, and a team around each child that includes a social worker, teachers and a therapist.

Councils and agencies set their own fees and support, and figures change from year to year, so ask each service what it pays today. Speaking to Foster4 and two or three of the agencies below, and comparing training, out-of-hours help and support groups, is a good way to find the right fit.
